comments.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 962 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/962).

compute_validity now records non-blocking registry_drift {signed,current} instead of returning stale-regver; the verdict is retired. ADR 0053 added (amends ADR 0015); ADR 0015, docs/plan-review-gate.md, attest_gate.py and manifest.py docstrings updated.

One finding during implementation, worth recording: removing the stale-regver verdict silently OPENED the progressive drift-refresh reuse path, because attest.drift_refresh_candidate had been relying on that verdict implicitly to deny reuse on registry skew. Caught by the existing interfaces test test_drift_refresh_skips_on_registry_skew. Fixed by an explicit registry_drift check in drift_refresh_candidate, and the seam is now documented in ADR 0053 -- claim gate grandfathers, reuse path stays conservative.

Gates: make lint + make typecheck clean; 6738 passed / 31 skipped across tests/unit + tests/interfaces. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before submit.

Asserts verdict == stale-code (with the message 'registry grandfathering must not mask real code drift') plus the registry_drift report riding along. Landing as Gerrit change 967 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/967). tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py: 11 passed.

compiled_state.description:
## Why

The plan-review claim gate invalidates a signed attestation whenever the criteria-registry
stamp (`regver:`) differs from the current one. `regver` hashes the FULL effective routing
index — including every criterion's free-text `check` string — so any edit to
`criteria_routing.json`, however cosmetic, rotates the stamp and invalidates EVERY
outstanding plan-review attestation repo-wide at once.

Measured on this repo: renaming one phrase in a single `check` string rotates the stamp
(`b058e30f0de6a907` -> `23913c1f6987711b`) and would invalidate the attestations held by
632 tickets (~40 open/in_progress), forcing a full LLM re-review before any of them can be
claimed. That is a false invalidation: the attestation truthfully certifies that the plan
passed the criteria AS THEY STOOD AT SIGNING TIME, and a later wording change does not
falsify that statement.

ADR 0015 introduced the check to stop a project activating/editing/disabling a criterion and
then claiming against a review that never saw it. The concern is real but the remedy is too
blunt: it cannot distinguish a criterion being tightened from a typo fix, so it charges a
full re-review for both. The result is that criteria maintenance is effectively frozen.

## What

Grandfather plan-review attestations across criteria-registry drift: a `regver` mismatch (or
a missing `regver:` line on an older manifest) no longer blocks the claim. The drift is still
DETECTED and REPORTED — it becomes advisory metadata on the validity result instead of a
blocking verdict — so `review-plan --status` and the gate UX can still say "reviewed under an
older criteria registry".

Explicitly unchanged: `stale-code`, `stale-head`, `stale-material`, `stale-reopened` and the
signature check all keep blocking. Only the registry-version dimension is grandfathered.

Also unchanged: the drift-refresh eligibility path (`registry_unchanged` in
`attest._signature_branch_decision` / `_sidecar_branch_decision` / `drift_floor`). That flag
decides whether a cheap refresh may REUSE a prior verdict versus running a full review; it
never blocks a claim, and keeping it conservative is correct.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — the plan-review branch of `compute_validity`
  (the `stale-regver` early return): stop returning `valid: False`; annotate the result.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — the docstring listing possible verdicts.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — `registry_version` docstring, which currently
  states a rotation invalidates a prior attestation.
- `docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md` — new ADR, amends ADR 0015.
- `docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` — add an amended-by pointer.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the two verdict lists that name `stale-regver`.
- Tests listed under Testing.

OUT OF SCOPE: the Success-Criteria -> Acceptance-Criteria rename itself (separate ticket);
any config surface for forcing re-review on a material criteria change (recorded as future
work in the ADR).

## Approach

In `compute_validity`'s `kind == _MANIFEST_PREFIX` branch, replace the early
`return _result(False, ..., "stale-regver")` with a non-blocking capture: compare the signed
`regver` against `registry_version(repo_root)` and, on mismatch or absence, record
`registry_drift = {"signed": ..., "current": ...}`. Let control fall through to the remaining
freshness checks (`stale-code` / `stale-head` / `stale-material`) unchanged. Attach
`registry_drift` to the returned dict via the existing `_result` helper so every downstream
result carries it uniformly.

The signed `regver` continues to be read from the AUTHENTICATED manifest (`auth_manifest`),
never its plaintext mirror — the reporting path must not become a channel for unauthenticated
data (ADR 0049 / the opcert binding tests).

## Testing

- `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py` — two cases currently asserting
  `verdict == "stale-regver"` invert to: valid, with `registry_drift` populated.
- `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` — same inversion for the overlay-change cases.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py` — the "no weakening" regver case becomes
  "grandfathered but reported"; the PLAINTEXT-corruption case must still prove the signed
  manifest is authoritative (unchanged assertion for `stale-code`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate_heldout.py` — drop `stale-regver` from the
  verdict->message mapping.
- NEW: a regression test proving a registry rotation alone leaves a claim UNBLOCKED while
  `stale-code` on the same attestation still blocks — pinning that only the registry
  dimension was grandfathered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plan-review attestation whose signed `regver` differs from the current
      `registry_version(repo_root)` returns `valid: True` from `compute_validity`, and the
      ticket can be claimed without a fresh `review-plan`.
- [ ] The same result carries `registry_drift` with the signed and current stamps, so the
      drift is reportable rather than silent.
- [ ] A manifest with NO `regver:` line is likewise grandfathered (valid), not rejected.
- [ ] `stale-code`, `stale-head`, `stale-material` and `stale-reopened` still return
      `valid: False` — proven by a test that rotates the registry AND drifts a dependency
      file on one attestation and asserts the verdict is `stale-code`.
- [ ] The signed `regver` is read from the authenticated manifest only; corrupting the
      plaintext mirror does not change the reported `registry_drift`.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md` exists, states the amendment to
      ADR 0015, and records the accepted consequence that a criteria TIGHTENING no longer
      retroactively forces re-review.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass, and the change carries Gerrit `Verified +1` (CI). Evidence for this criterion is a gate RUN, which leaves no artifact in the codebase; it is attested by the recorded CI vote and command output on this ticket.
